parity.text: Write a Python function that parses lines like '07:14:03 | cam C07 | lane 2 | truck count=12 | avg_speed=41 | occupancy=55% | event=stall' into a dict with typed fields. Include a short docstring and one example call.

A sensor reports vehicle counts of 12, 15, 9, 31, 14 over five consecutive minutes. The 4th reading triggers an alert if it exceeds 1.8 times the mean of the other four. Does it trigger? Show the calculation.
Explain to a city traffic engineer, in plain language, what a mixture-of-experts language model is and why it can run on a laptop-class chip. Keep it under 150 words.

Return a JSON object describing a traffic incident with fields: id, timestamp (ISO 8601), camera, severity (low/medium/high), lanes_blocked (integer), description. Make up realistic values for a stalled truck on I-84 eastbound at 07:42.
List eight concrete things an edge AI appliance at an intersection could do with a vision-language model, one line each.

If a corridor carries 1,850 vehicles per hour at an average of 1.2 occupants per vehicle, and a 20-minute full closure occurs, roughly how many people are delayed? Then estimate total person-minutes lost if each is delayed 20 minutes. Show steps.
Translate into Spanish and Japanese: 'Lane 2 is closed ahead due to a stalled vehicle. Merge left and reduce speed.'
Write a 120-word vignette, in a calm documentary tone, about a night-shift operator watching an empty highway at 3 a.m. when a single wrong-way driver appears on camera 17.
